new_commodity_proposals.evidence: A bagged frozen riced-cauliflower product, 1,190 g at batch scale, so a material purchase and not a garnish. Nothing on the pre-resolve table prices it: the board's only offer was `rice` (a different food) and the near vocabulary rows were all rice. It is NOT the live `cauliflower` id - that is a fresh head, and fresh-is-not-frozen is a standing estate rejection with a different price per pound and a different gram yield. The estate already mints frozen-vegetable ids separately from their fresh twins: `frozen-broccoli-florets` is used by another recipe in this very batch. If an id already prices bagged frozen riced cauliflower under another spelling (frozen-riced-cauliflower, cauliflower-rice), alias it and I withdraw.

registrar_rulings.reason: No id prices frozen riced cauliflower under any spelling: 'cauliflower' (fresh head, each, $1.98 Fareway) explicitly excludes frozen/rice/riced, and 'frozen-cauliflower-florets' (itself unpriced today) explicitly excludes riced cauliflower and cauliflower rice, so the estate deliberately carved this product out of both existing ids rather than carrying it; no 'riced' string exists in the feed, the alias map, or recipe-board-everyday. Same food as 'cauliflower' but different form (frozen riced vs fresh head) - a different purchase, per the frozen-broccoli-florets precedent. FOLLOW-UP EDITS: mint in commodities.json (weekly staples, unit oz) with include '^(?=.*\bfrozen\b)(?=.*\b(?:cauliflower\s+rice|riced\s+cauliflower)\b).*$'; clone frozen-cauliflower-florets' full exclude block (~150 patterns incl. baby-food/pet/beverage) and add excludes for florets, pizza/crust, stir-fry/vegetable blends and seasoned/flavored medleys; add commodity-dupe-allowlist.json pairs frozen-cauliflower-rice<->cauliflower (fresh vs frozen form), frozen-cauliflower-rice<->frozen-cauliflower-florets (riced vs florets cut - shared 'frozen-cauliflower-' prefix will trip the audit's prefix rule), and frozen-cauliflower-rice<->rice (cauliflower is not a grain). Note to caller: id will EXIST but is NOT PRICED - it needs a capture-worklist entry before the recipe costs. Vocabulary is a separate ruling: 'cooked frozen cauliflower rice' needs its own ingredients.json row (no densities/macros row exists; FDC 168521 'Cauliflower, frozen, cooked, boiled, drained, with salt' is the plausible macro source but transcribe/verify a bag label per the agreement-is-not-identity rule) - this approval mints the id only, not the name.
